subject: Draft: Joint Acceptance Roadmap & Eval Timeline (Atlas.ai)
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Amy Chen <amy@atlas.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: Joint Acceptance Roadmap & Eval Timeline (Atlas.ai)

Hi Amy —

Good to meet earlier this week. Per our conversation, attached is a lightweight starter for a Joint Acceptance Roadmap (JAR) and a 2-slide summary that frames the evaluation milestones. The goal is to give both teams a clear, timeboxed set of actions so the technical trial and procurement can run in parallel.

Key draft milestones (proposal):
- Week 0 (Jul 6): Technical kickoff + credentials & test data access
- Week 1–2: Integration & smoke tests (Redwood SE + Atlas engineers)
- Week 2: Pilot run with sampled traffic (performance / cost checks)
- Week 3: Acceptance criteria review (accuracy, latency, infra) + security checklist sign-off
- Week 4 (target Jul 31): Decision milestone / PO issuance or next steps

As a starting point I uploaded: joint_acceptance_roadmap_gdoc (editable) and a short MAP_2slide_summary.pdf. Links below.

Ask: can you share the preferred stakeholders for technical sign-off, security, and procurement so we can add owners to the JAR table? Also let me know if you have a procurement window or DocuSign preferences — happy to accommodate.

I cc'd Marissa (Customer Success) and Neha (Security/compliance lead) so they can add operational and audit items into the doc. If this looks good, we can run a 30-min sync next week (I have Tue/Wed afternoons open).

Links/attachments: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-JointAcceptanceRoadmap (editable)
https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1xYz-MAP-2slide-summary

Thanks,
David Kim
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: joint_acceptance_roadmap_gdoc_link.txt (Google Doc link stub), MAP_2slide_summary.pdf (2 slides, PDF)

From: Amy Chen <amy@atlas.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Singh <r.singh@atlas.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Joint Acceptance Roadmap & Eval Timeline (Atlas.ai)

David — thanks for the fast follow and the doc. I skimmed the starter MAP and like the alignment. A few requests from our side before we lock dates: 

1) Security/compliance: we need a clear slot for our security team to review SOC2 evidence and the data retention plan. Can Neha share a short checklist / expected artifacts?
2) Acceptance criteria: can we add an item measuring end-to-end latency at 95th percentile (our SLA gating)? Also include example test cases for model hallucination checks.
3) Procurement: our procurement team typically needs 10 business days to process a PO and we prefer DocuSign. I cc'd Rajiv (ops) to confirm.

Happy to run a 30-min working session. Tue/Thu next week are better for us in the morning (PDT).

Best,
Amy Chen
Product Lead, Atlas.ai

Amy / David — thanks for the notes. I've pulled the MAP into an editable draft and added two short tabs: 

- Mutual actions (owner / due date / status) — I filled initial owners for the tech and CS workstreams
- Risk & gating (security, data retention, acceptance tests) — Neha, I added a placeholder for SOC2 evidence links and an expected turn-around for our side.

Proposed small adjustments to milestones (keeping the same rhythm):
- Week 0 (Jul 6): Kickoff + temporary test creds (owner: Atlas eng)
- Week 1: Integration QA + baseline performance capture (owner: Redwood SE)
- Week 2: Pilot with sampled traffic + 95th pctl latency check (owner: joint)
- Week 2–3: Security review & sign-off (owner: Neha / Atlas security)
- Week 4 (target Jul 31): Acceptance review & procurement handoff (owner: Rajiv / Atlas procurement)

Neha — can you paste the minimal SOC2 artifacts we can provide and the approximate lead-time? We'll add them to the doc under Risk & gating.

Amy — I dropped two suggested test cases in the Acceptance section (hallucination detection + factuality sample) and a quick example of the latency measurement. If the procurement window is 10 business days, that fits with the July 31 target as long as PO reads arrive by July 17. Please confirm.

I added a short meeting poll in the doc — David, can you pick Tue AM or Thu AM next week?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
